item.title: New city roles point to Sheffield’s focus on youth and education in Detroit
item.description: Detroit Mayor, Mary Sheffield, speaks with high school students during her first visit after being sworn into office on Fri., Jan. 9, 2026 at Pershing High School in Detroit. This week, she announced two new roles related to youth affairs and education in her administration.

item.title: Engineer or entrepreneur? NYC parents want career aptitude assessments for high schoolers
item.description: Students in a journalism class at Brooklyn's High School for Global Citizenship on Sept. 11, 2025. Some parents are pushing for all high schoolers to take career aptitude assessments.

item.title: Detroit school district is spending millions to increase security after safety concerns
item.description: The Detroit district's board voted to hire 38 more security guards weeks after a student reportedly chased a peer with a boxcutter in class at Denby High School. Pictured are the metal detectors at the entrance of Pershing High School.

item.title: African American Coalition: Parents of color ‘not a monolith’ in supporting IPS overhaul
item.description: Pastor Clyde Posley, Jr., with fellow clergy members behind him, speaks against the Indianapolis Local Education Alliance's recommendation that will dilute the power of the elected school board ahead of the group's final vote in December. Multiple members of the Black community have expressed concern with the recommendations, many of which are adopted in House Bill 1423.

item.title: Some board members claim ‘sabotage’ as Chicago school board and search firm tasked with finding new CEO part ways
item.description: Chicago Public Schools interim CEO Macquline King, right, listens during a school board meeting last year. The school board has terminated its contract with its search firm, and now a handful of board members are calling for the district to keep King in place until a new board is seated next year.

item.title: Misdemeanor convictions wouldn’t prevent some Colorado teachers from getting hired if new bill passes
item.description: Colorado lawmakers don't want older misdemeanors to hold back educators from getting a license.

item.title: Philadelphia wants to entice students back to neighborhood high schools. Will it work?
item.description: Paul Robeson High School in West Philadelphia is one of five magnet or citywide admissions high schools the district wants to close. District officials say they want to reinvest in neighborhood high schools.

item.title: Education bill tracker: Indiana lawmakers advance bills on Indianapolis schools, cellphones, and more
item.description: New Indiana bills propose changes to cellphone policies and social media.

item.title: ICE detained her students. This Minnesota superintendent couldn’t keep quiet.
item.description: Children hold signs on the stoop of a house in Minneapolis as protesters march against ICE. A surge of immigration enforcement in the Twin Cities has had wide-ranging effects on schools and children.

item.title: NYC spent $1.6 billion shielding schools from enrollment losses. Will Mamdani keep it up?
item.description: NYC has spent $1.6 billion in recent years cushioning schools from enrollment-related cuts. As Mamdani warns of a $7 billion budget gap, the mayor has yet to say what he’ll do. His preliminary budget is due next week.
